items: 4.1 T1 install into a repo that already has a config — activation is the adopter's paste, and it is a precondition rather than a step that can lag the store
4.1 T2 upgrade — `init` cannot deliver one; the mechanism is adopter deletion of the reinstall unit followed by reinstall, terminating over a finite enumerable set
4.1 T3 upgrade with a deliberately edited file — survives an install by the additive-only contract; destroyed by the default upgrade path, and pinned at the old version permanently if spared by hand
4.1 T4 add / remove an adapter — the previous file keeps working until a human deletes it; discovery is by re-render or banner signature, and neither covers the unbannered codex snippet
4.1 T5 rename the store directory — the old tree is discoverable only by content, and the adapters keep pointing at it because the reinstall skips them
4.1 T6 remove the config block — recorded limit in its narrow form: no durable pointer survives, a content search still works
4.1 T7 the receipt's own second write — no receipt exists and this model introduces none; if one ever is, `init` is its only writer and it is not itself a destination
4.3 the model as a whole: `_docs/design/prompt-store-state-model.md`, including its six recorded limits and their design/mixed classification
acceptances.reason: owner read the seven transition answers and the six recorded limits as presented in session and approved them explicitly, which unblocks PRD-034. What the machine established is narrow and is recorded as such: the §11 gates hold the document's structure only (all seven transitions present, all four axes non-blank, discrimination proved by blanking an axis and observing exit 1), and the independent review caught three factual errors about the shipped installer — a banner premise false for the codex adapter, a T3 that answered the install instead of the upgrade, and a T6 limit its own sibling transition refuted — with all nine findings fixed in the files rather than waived. No gate can establish that these are the right design decisions, which is exactly what this row records. Two disclosures the owner accepted with the decision: the reviewer was a fresh same-family session with zero implementation context, the method's documented fallback rather than its different-model-family default, and this same session wrote the PRD, scored it, planned it and authored the deliverable. Written by the agent at the owner's explicit in-session approval, under ADR-0003.
